def test_iniconfig_strips_utf8_bom(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    # Windows editors often write a UTF-8 BOM; it must not break the first section.
    p = tmp_path / "bom.ini"
    p.write_bytes(b"\xef\xbb\xbf[section]\nkey = value\n")
    assert IniConfig(str(p))["section"]["key"] == "value"

    p = tmp_path / "bom.ini"
    p.write_bytes(b"\xef\xbb\xbf[section]\nkey = value\n")
    assert IniConfig.parse(str(p))["section"]["key"] == "value"
EOF

`parse_ini_data` in `src/iniconfig/_parse.py` now strips a leading UTF-8 BOM. `IniConfig()` and `IniConfig.parse()` both go through it, so one strip covers both. I added two tests in `testing/test_iniconfig.py`, one for each entry point, that read a BOM-prefixed file.

The suite passes when I run it with `PYTHONPATH=src` (53 passed, including the two new tests). The owned `ep_check.py` run failed, though. It runs plain `python -m pytest testing -q`, and pytest crashes on import in that environment with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'iniconfig'`. The package isn't installed there. My own plain run of that command hit the same error. The failure is the environment, not the change. An editable install (`pip install -e .`) into that venv would probably fix it, but I haven't done that.
